tool.name: pathotypr train
tool.description: fits a Random Forest lineage classifier on labelled genomes

param.name: input
param.label: Labelled genomes
param.help: A FASTA whose headers carry the class label. See the warning below about how the label is read.

param.name: method
param.label: How to estimate accuracy
param.help: The final model is trained on all of the data either way. This only changes how the accuracy figure is obtained.

param.label: Number of folds
param.help: Must not exceed the number of samples. Preferable to a single split on small or imbalanced sets.

param.label: Maximum tree depth
param.help: Lower values reduce overfitting on small datasets.

param.label: Minimum samples per leaf
param.help: Higher values act as regularisation, stopping a tree memorising individual genomes.

param.name: want_reports
param.label: Also output the feature importance reports
param.help: Which hash buckets the forest split on most, and where the k-mers behind them sit in the training sequences.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`pathotypr train` turns a labelled set of genomes into a Random Forest that *pathotypr predict* can then apply to new sequences. Each sequence is hashed into a fixed-size k-mer feature vector, so there is no vocabulary to fit and the features at prediction time are identical to those at training time by construction.
The accuracy figure it reports comes either from a single held-out split or from stratified cross-validation. Either way the **model it saves is trained on all of your data**; the split only exists to produce the estimate. An out-of-bag accuracy is also computed from the bootstrap samples and costs nothing extra.
.. class:: warningmark
**The label is the first whitespace-separated token of the FASTA header.** Everything after the first space is ignored. This is the single most common mistake with this tool: genomes downloaded from a public archive keep headers like ``>GCF_000195955.2 Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv``, which yields one class per accession rather than one class per group, and nothing warns you. Rewrite the headers to the labels you actually want predicted::
>L2 sample_A collected_2021 >L2 sample_B >L4.3 sample_C
Labels are compared as flat strings. ``L4`` and ``L4.1`` are two unrelated classes; the tool knows nothing about the hierarchy in the name. If you want hierarchical calls, use a marker panel with *pathotypr classify* or *pathotypr split-fastq* instead.
**How much data**
Nothing enforces a minimum per class, but a class represented by one or two genomes contributes almost nothing the forest can generalise from. Aim for ten or more per class, and prefer cross-validation over a single split when the set is small or imbalanced.
@ORGANISM_NOTE@
